fixes.explanation: That's it, friend. The LORD says, "…you are to divide the land by lot according to your clans." (Numbers 33:54). Then He adds, "Whatever falls to each one by lot will be his." So the lot is what settles each share, and nobody has to guess whose it is.

Teaching them is a thoughtful idea, friend. Here, though, the text gives a different instruction: "…you must drive out before you all the inhabitants of the land…" (Numbers 33:52). Teaching them isn't part of what the LORD tells Moses to say here. Sometimes the answer is just what the sentence says, and this sentence says drive out.

That's right, it's false. The LORD says Israel must "…demolish all their high places." (Numbers 33:52). He lists it right alongside their carved images and cast idols. The instruction is to take the high places down, so no leaving a few up for decoration.

Right on the money. The LORD says, "…for I have given you the land to possess." (Numbers 33:53). The reason is that He gave it, plain and simple. When the LORD hands you the keys, that's the whole reason, friend.

True! The LORD says, "Give a larger inheritance to a larger clan and a smaller inheritance to a smaller one." (Numbers 33:54). The size of the clan matters for the size of the share. Bigger clan, bigger share. Smaller clan, smaller share.

I see why you'd think that, friend, because the wilderness sounds like a natural next stop. But the LORD doesn't say that here. He says, "And then I will do to you what I had planned to do to them." (Numbers 33:56). Sending Israel back to the wilderness isn't in that sentence.

Yes, friend! The LORD says, "Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun." (Numbers 34:17). Eleazar is a priest, and Joshua is named as the son of Nun. Two names on the job list, and then He tells Moses to appoint one leader from each tribe to help distribute the land (Numbers 34:18). That's a whole team, and I'd want my name on that list.

Phinehas and Hur are good names, friend, but they aren't the ones the LORD gives here. He says the men to assign the land are "Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun." (Numbers 34:17). One is a priest and the other is the son of Nun. This passage has a lot of names, so it's easy to mix them up. I'd need a sticky note.

Nice try, friend! But the LORD names someone else. He says the men to assign the land are "Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun." (Numbers 34:17). Bezalel and Eldad aren't named in this passage. Those two are the ones for this job.
